### problem_chain

Walked from the root using the policy rules and the raw DB alone.

The customer asks for one thing: move the spare money out of the money market into her checking account.
That is `savings_ext_surplus_transfer_amount` (`trigger: on_request`, `subject: savings_withdrawal`).
Its `rule` carries exactly one sentence saying what its result waits on:

> "The surplus available to move out is fixed only after the credit owed for the excess withdrawal fees
> charged on branch and ATM withdrawals stands on the account."

Finding the write that brings that state about, as a reader must: two tools in this difficulty post a
`savings_fee_refund`. `credit_savings_courtesy_refund_0ed102a0` is governed by
`savings_ext_periodic_fee_courtesy_credit`, whose rule books its entry *"against the most recently posted
monthly maintenance fee on the account"*; `credit_savings_fee_review_ce0a6323` is governed by
`savings_ext_excess_fee_review_credit`, whose rule books *"a review credit for the excess withdrawal fees
charged against withdrawals that never counted toward the allowance"* against *"the most recently posted
excess withdrawal fee"*. Only the second answers excess withdrawal fees. The hop has one reading.
`savings_ext_excess_fee_review_credit.rule` carries no prerequisite sentence, so the walk stops.

**Derived tree** (identical to the declared one):

```
savings_ext_surplus_transfer_amount                 [root, owner=user write]
└── value_input (settled_balance) ── savings_ext_excess_fee_review_credit
```

n = 1 prerequisite problem (within 1–3), 1 `value_input` edge (floor is max(1−1,1) = 1), no cycle.

**Why the edge is false at the opening — DB row evidence.** The condition is that the ledger carries a
credit entry answering those excess withdrawal fees. `initial_state.savings_transactions` holds 17 rows
and **not one** has `event_type = "savings_fee_refund"`; the event types present are `savings_deposit`
(3), `savings_fee` (4), `savings_withdrawal` (6) and `savings_interest_credit` (3). `refunds_all` is
therefore 0.00 at the opening. Genuinely unmet, and unmet in the strongest way — the state is not merely
partial, it is wholly absent.

Unlike task 0's promotional edge (see `_difficulty.md`, **CG-6**), this edge's declared `condition` — *"The
account's ledger carries a credit entry answering the excess withdrawal fees charged against withdrawals
made in person at a branch or at an ATM, so the settled balance already includes it"* — is neither
stronger nor weaker than its `policy_source` sentence, and is false at the opening on the rows above.

**Per-edge load-bearing run.** Skipping the review credit and replaying the root unchanged:

| run | review credit | `settled_balance` | root result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| full chain | 24.00 | 44,373.46 | **16,530.00** |
| skip the review credit | — | 44,349.46 | 16,512.00 |

The edge moves the scored parameter by 18.00. It is not decorative. (The 24.00 credit propagates through
`settled_balance` → `available_basis` → `surplus` → `× 0.75` → `offset_surplus`, so 24.00 × 0.75 = 18.00
reaches the result.)

**Parallel edges.** The root has one out-edge, so no parallel-order ambiguity can arise.

**No waiting.** The single prerequisite is resolved by one synchronous agent write, as set out above.

**The tool layer does not judge the prerequisite.** `credit_savings_fee_review_ce0a6323` and
`transfer_savings_surplus_c4c79a83` were read in full in
`env/regional_retail_bank/tasks/savings_withdrawals_interest_and_transfers/task_tools.py`. Each executes
unconditionally: `rid = ctx.make_id(...)`, `ctx.create("savings_transactions", …)`, a re-sum of the
account's rows into `savings_accounts.current_balance`, and a formatted return. Neither raises, refuses,
returns an error, nor emits a hint about the other. `transfer_savings_surplus_c4c79a83` in particular does
not check the retained balance, the daily limit or the allowance — all of those remain the agent's
judgement.

**A customer's own write is in the tree.** The root's `target_tool` `transfer_savings_surplus_c4c79a83` is
declared `@tool(owner="user", rw="write")`, and the persona hands it over passively: *"Once the
representative has worked the figure out and hands the transfer over for you to authorise, you run it with
the amount they give you… You will not run anything before it is handed to you and you will not ask to be
handed it."* PASS.

**Isomorphism.** The derived tree matches the declared `prerequisite` graph node for node, edge for edge
and kind for kind; the topological order — review credit, then surplus transfer — is forced.

### factor_weight

Two computations, 10 declared factors. Every figure is the auditor's own recomputation on that problem's
handling-time world.

**`savings_ext_excess_fee_review_credit` — reference result 24.00.**

| factor | effect | honest? | tier taken and the rows that put her there | `baseline` | recomputed under the baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reviewable_pool_width` | method | yes — changes the window the fees are drawn from | top: `card_purchase_count_year = 6 >= 6` and `rewards_balance = 4,150 >= 3,000` | `reviewable_fee_pool = excess_fees_one_month` = 10.00, which is exactly what `baseline.rule` states ("the excess withdrawal fees posted to the account in the one calendar month ending on the review date") | **10.00** |
| `covered_fee_units` | parameter | yes — a count | top: `fee_count_twelve_month = 5 >= 5` and `months_since_opening = 31 <= 36` | `covered_fee_units = K('fee_units_standard')` = 1, matching "The review covers one fee unit" | **10.00** |
| `review_ceiling_step` | parameter | yes — a dollar ceiling | top: checking `ledger_balance = 1,850 < 5,000` and direct deposits `820 < 1,000` | `review_ceiling = K('review_ceiling_standard')` = 60.00, matching "The review ceiling is 60.00 USD" | **30.00** |
| `ceiling_bite_moment` | method | yes — changes where the cap is applied | middle: `withdrawal_count_three_month = 3`, ≥ 2 and < 4 | `capped_review_credit = raw_review_credit` = 30.00, matching "the fee units alone govern the credit booked" | **30.00** |

All four bear weight. All four baselines are exactly what `baseline.rule` states for that input — none is a
straw man, and each factor's fall-through tier is the baseline. Substituting all four at once gives
**10.00**, a definite number and not gold: a reader with only the computation document arrives at
`MN(10.00, 1 × 10.00)` = 10.00, wrong by 14.00.

Counts: 4 factors (at the lower bound), 2 `parameter`, 2 `method`, 3 multi-source
(`reviewable_pool_width`: `card_transactions` purchase count **and** `card_accounts.rewards_balance`;
`covered_fee_units`: the savings fee count **and** `savings_accounts.opened_date`; `review_ceiling_step`:
`checking_accounts.ledger_balance` **and** `checking_transactions` direct deposits), 2 cross-difficulty
(card, checking). Within bounds.

**`savings_ext_surplus_transfer_amount` — reference result 16,530.00.**

| factor | effect | tier taken | `baseline` | recomputed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fresh_deposit_hold` | method | top: card owes 3,420.75 ≥ 2,000 and rewards 4,150 < 10,000 | `available_basis = settled_balance`, matching "The available balance is the settled balance" | **21,030.00** |
| `retained_balance_cushion` | parameter | top: checking 1,850 < 2,500 and direct deposits 820 < 1,000 | `retained_target = P('waiver_min_daily_balance')` = 10,000, matching "the tier's minimum daily balance waiver threshold" | **20,280.00** |
| `moved_surplus_share` | parameter | top: 3 withdrawals in three months ≥ 3 and 31 ≤ 36 months open | `surplus_share = K('share_standard')` = 1.0, matching "the whole surplus is moved" | **22,373.00** |
| `recent_withdrawal_offset` | method | top: `withdrawals_one_month = 2,900 ≥ 2,000` | `offset_surplus = paced_surplus`, matching "No withdrawal already posted is set against it" | **17,530.00** |
| `moved_amount_rounding` | method | top: `interest_row_count_year = 3 ≥ 3` | `rounded_amount = RND(offset_surplus, 2)`, matching "rounded half up to the cent" | **16,530.10** |
| `transfer_ceiling_step` | parameter | top: `deposit_count_year = 2 ≥ 2` | `transfer_ceiling = K('ceiling_standard')` = 5,000, matching "never more than the transfer ceiling of 5,000.00 USD" | **5,000.00** |

All six bear weight; `moved_amount_rounding` only by 0.10, but the scored value does change.
Substituting all six at once gives **5,000.00** ≠ 16,530.00 — a definite, wrong fall-back number.

Counts: 6 factors, 3 `parameter`, 3 `method`, 2 multi-source (`fresh_deposit_hold`:
`card_accounts.current_balance` **and** `rewards_balance`; `retained_balance_cushion`:
`checking_accounts.ledger_balance` **and** `checking_transactions` direct deposits), 2 cross-difficulty
(card, checking). Within bounds.

**Cross-difficulty evidence is seeded.** `checking_accounts` (1 row, Everyday Checking,
`ledger_balance = 1,850.00`), `checking_transactions` (3 rows, one of them an ACH direct deposit in the
window), `card_accounts` (1 row, Travel Rewards Visa Signature, `current_balance = 3,420.75`,
`rewards_balance = 4,150`), `card_transactions` (8 rows, 7 purchases and 1 payment). None of the four
cross-reads returns absent, and each holding is consistent with its own product charter.

**No tier is read off a stamp.** Every tier above rests on a history aggregate, a date span or a
cross-category balance. The stamp-shaped fields on this seed — `savings_accounts.promo_end_date`
(2024-08-15, long expired), `last_customer_activity_date`, `card_accounts.penalty_apr_active` — name none
of these outcomes and are read by no binding. `savings_accounts.current_balance` (44,349.46) agrees with
`settled_balance` before the review credit, but no binding reads it: both policies recompute the balance
from the ledger rows, so the field cannot substitute for the rule.

**Near-misses.** Present in both computations, and score-distinguishing in three places:

- *decisive* — `checking_transactions` carries an ACH direct deposit of **2,600.00 on 2026-05-30**, which
  falls one window-step outside the three calendar months ending 2026-09-16
  (`MONTHS(2026-05-30, 2026-09-16) = 3`). A careless reader counts it, gets
  `checking_direct_deposits = 3,420.00 >= 1,000.00`, and lands on the **18.00** review ceiling instead of
  24.00 — scoring 18.00 rather than 24.00 for the credit — and on a `retained_target` of 12,000.00 instead
  of 15,000.00, scoring 18,780.00 rather than 16,530.00 for the transfer. The rule sentences that exclude
  it are *"received less than 1,000.00 USD of direct deposits in the three calendar months ending on the
  review date"* and the same phrase in the surplus rule.
- *decisive* — the 2026-06-10 `wire_out` fee of 20.00 is a `savings_fee` but not an excess withdrawal fee.
  A reader who takes "fee entries" to mean excess fees gets `fee_count_twelve_month = 4`, drops
  `covered_fee_units` to 2, and scores `MN(24.00, 20.00)` = 20.00 instead of 24.00. The rule says
  *"five or more fee entries posted to the account"* — every fee, not only excess ones.
- *present but not tier-flipping* — the 2026-06-10 wire withdrawal of 12,000.00 sits just outside the
  three-month withdrawal window (`MONTHS = 3`); counting it would move `ceiling_bite_moment` to its top
  tier, which happens to give 24.00 as well. Likewise the 2024-10-02 card purchase (outside twelve months)
  and the 2024-02-15 opening deposit (outside twelve months) leave their tiers unchanged. Recorded for
  completeness.

**Factor verdict.** All 10 declared factors bear weight against honest baselines, every ladder has three
disjoint tiers stated in full in its rule, both computations are within the structural bounds, and each
all-baseline fall-back is a definite number different from gold. PASS.

## findings

**F1-1 — observation: the root's prerequisite sentence is narrower than the policy it routes to.**

- *Symptom.* `savings_ext_surplus_transfer_amount`'s prerequisite sentence waits on the credit for "the
  excess withdrawal fees charged on **branch and ATM** withdrawals", while
  `savings_ext_excess_fee_review_credit` scopes itself to "the excess withdrawal fees charged against
  **withdrawals that never counted toward the allowance**".
- *Root cause.* Base `savings_evt_withdrawal_allowance` makes branch and ATM withdrawals a proper subset
  of the uncounted ones — a withdrawal through a channel outside the tier's
  `excess_withdrawal_counted_channels` also never counts — so the sentence names a strict subset of the
  depended-on policy's subject. See `_difficulty.md`, `### findings`, CG-7.
- *Evidence.* `savings.extended.yaml`, `savings_ext_surplus_transfer_amount.rule` sentence 2 against
  `savings_ext_excess_fee_review_credit.rule` sentence 1; base
  `savings_evt_withdrawal_allowance.rule`, "Withdrawals made in person at a branch or at an ATM never
  count toward the allowance."
- *Consequence.* None on this task. All four excess fee rows name branch or ATM withdrawals as their
  `source_item_id` (table in `### policy_self_consistency (this task only)`), so both scopes select the
  same four fees, the same 50.00 pool and the same 24.00 credit. The hop still resolves to exactly one
  write. Observation, not a red light.
- *Affected artifact and location.* `savings.extended.yaml`, `savings_ext_surplus_transfer_amount.rule`
  and `prerequisite[0].policy_source` / `.condition`.
- *Relation to previous revisions.* First revision; no prior audit of this difficulty exists.

**F1-2 — observation: `savings_ext_excess_fee_review_credit` sits at the minimum on every structural
count.** Four factors (floor 4), two `parameter` (floor 2), two `method` (floor 2), two cross-difficulty
(floor 2). Every one bears weight on this world against an honest baseline and the all-baseline fall-back
of 10.00 is a definite wrong number, so nothing fails; recorded only because the computation has no margin
— striking out any single factor would put it below the bound.

**F1-3 — observation: `moved_amount_rounding` bears weight by 0.10.** Substituting its baseline
(`RND(offset_surplus, 2)`) moves the scored transfer from 16,530.00 to 16,530.10. The scored value does
change, so the factor is load-bearing and the test passes; the margin is a tenth of a dollar out of
sixteen thousand, which is worth knowing when the ladder is rendered into a document a solver must find.

**F1-4 — observation: two near-misses on this task do not distinguish a tier.** The 2026-06-10 wire
withdrawal (just outside the three-month window) would move `ceiling_bite_moment` to its top tier, which
also yields 24.00; the 2024-10-02 card purchase and the 2024-02-15 opening deposit (both outside twelve
months) leave their tiers unchanged. The requirement is met twice over by decisive near-misses — the
2026-05-30 checking direct deposit of 2,600.00, which would change both the review ceiling (24.00 → 18.00)
and the retained target (15,000.00 → 12,000.00), and the 2026-06-10 `wire_out` fee, which a reader who
takes "fee entries" to mean excess fees alone would omit, dropping `covered_fee_units` from 3 to 2 and the
credit from 24.00 to 20.00. No red light.

**Not attributed to any solving agent.** This task's derivation reproduced GT exactly on every item; the
observations above concern the artifacts' wording and margins, not any agent's behaviour.
